messages:
sam: FYI — I'm seeing weird spikes in error budget burn on the SLO dashboard this morning for eu-west GPU pools. Anyone else?

mira: same, noticed it ~07:12 UTC. Grafana shows redwood_gpu_pool_saturation jumping then settling. Looks like aggregation artifacts to me.

ravi: quick clarifying Q — are the region SLOs computed as request-weighted aggregates or simple averages across pools? That changes the interpretation a lot.

sam: I think infra dashboards are averaging pool SLIs, while product SLOs elsewhere are request-weighted. That's probably why eu-west looks worse here than in the product dashboard.

opsbot: automated-report: weekly-burn: eu-west: 7.8% (30d rolling), us-west: 1.2%, ap-south: 0.9% :rotating_light: — see /reports/slo-weekly.csv

julia: Proposal: for region-level SLI we should weight by request volume (sum of good requests / sum of total requests). Keep per-pool SLIs for debugging. Also: use a 5m window for latency SLI, but 1m for saturation alerts.

mira: +1 on weighting. Caveat: tiny pools with low qps could be hidden if we only use region-weighted metrics. We should have a min-sample floor and default to per-pool SLOs if samples < X.

ravi: Agreed. Also looking at PromQL — current error rate query used in some panels is:
```
avg(rate(redwood_inference_errors_total[5m])) by (pool) / avg(rate(redwood_inference_requests_total[5m])) by (pool)
```
That avg() by pool will create the exact problem. We want: 
```
sum(rate(redwood_inference_errors_total[5m])) by (region) / sum(rate(redwood_inference_requests_total[5m])) by (region)
```
to get request-weighted region SLIs.

sam: OK that explains it. Some of our region panels were set up as simple avg() panels for visual parity across pools. We should switch region panels to the sum/rate form and keep the avg() per-pool panels for troubleshooting.

mira: For error budget reporting cadence — do we keep calendar-month buckets (ties to billing) or switch to rolling 30d for operational readings? My vote is rolling 30d for burn, calendar month for billing reconciliation.

julia: Rolling 30d is more actionable for on-call. Also propose smoothing the burn-rate signal with a 6h median or 3h expo-smooth to avoid alerts on brief load tests.

ravi: Small note on SLI windows: switching from a 1m to 5m window for saturation will reduce sensitivity but also reduce false positives during short scheduler spikes. We should document the trade-offs.

sam: Action items: 1) Update Grafana region panels to use sum/rate by region (ravi/mira) 2) Add per-pool min-sample floor and a per-pool SLO panel (mira) 3) Update burn-report to use 30d rolling + smoothing and keep a calendar-month view for billing (ravi) 4) Add runbook note about interpretation and small-pool caveat (julia). Who can take ownership?

mira: I'll take the Grafana edits and per-pool floor. Will open PR against infra-dashboards, target EOD.

ravi: I'll update the burn-report script and add smoothing, and change the region panels' queries to sum/rate where needed. PR + tests tomorrow morning.

julia: I'll add the runbook section and a short blurb in the SLO docs about weighting vs averaging.

opsbot: rollout-log: dashboards/pr-542 opened by mira, burn-report/pr-88 opened by ravi. Scheduled apply: 2026-03-19 09:00 UTC.

sam: thanks team :thumbsup: Once PRs land let's watch eu-west for one full business day and confirm burn drops below 5% before closing the incident.

mira: noted — will post a follow-up when panels are live.

ravi: one more thought — add an automated alert that flags if weighted region SLI and unweighted mean differ by >2%. That will catch config drift.

sam: good idea, add it to the dashboard tests.

mira: will include that in the Grafana test suite PR.

sam: closing the thread for now, will reopen if we see continued high burn. Thanks.
